about: DM layer for the Connections view (prime/timeline). Hand-kept. Nodes reuse record ids where the entity is in data/.

nodes.label: The Prime Continuum
nodes.summary: All of existence, one thing with Continuity: every galaxy, the Astral Sea between, and Rykoe at the center.

facts.t: Continuity and the Prime Continuum are one thing: all of existence.
Every galaxy, system, world and plane lies inside it.
The cosmos is a collective of five galaxies arranged around Rykoe at its center.

nodes.label: Continuity
nodes.summary: The interplay of the five Axioms: reality itself, one thing with the Prime Continuum.

facts.t: Continuity runs both ways: it rises out of the Axioms, and whoever reaches into it can push and pull them and remake reality.
Continuity preserves itself: when a world is pushed to an extreme, it answers with a Monolith.
Its present form dates from the Reach.

nodes.label: The Axioms
nodes.summary: The five laws that govern how energy behaves: Consolidation, Expansion, Dissolution, Distinction and Determination.

facts.t: Energy has always existed; it is never made or destroyed, only arranged.
Consolidation and Expansion decide where energy goes; Dissolution and Distinction decide what form it takes; Determination keeps outcomes open.
Continuity is the interplay of the five: reality itself.

nodes.label: Consolidation
nodes.summary: The Axiom that draws things together.

facts.t: Consolidation draws energy together into clouds, stars, worlds and galaxies.
Where Consolidation wins outright with Dissolution, it collapses into a core.
Consolidation and Dissolution close possibilities; Expansion and Distinction open them.
The Rod of Seven Parts is the Consolidation fragment.

nodes.label: Dissolution
nodes.summary: The Axiom that mixes everything into sameness, until nothing stands apart.

facts.t: Every pocket of difference sends more sameness out into the cosmos than it keeps.
Time runs one way because of Dissolution.
The twins carry the Dissolution fragment, two pieces.

nodes.label: Distinction
nodes.summary: The Axiom that makes and keeps things different.

facts.t: Distinction builds and holds distinct things in the flow of energy: elements, weather, life, minds.
A Zenith is the moment a world reaches its peak of Distinction; it happens, a Monolith answers, and it does not continue.
Every Distinction piece finds or reveals something, telling one thing apart from everything else.

nodes.label: Determination
nodes.summary: The Axiom by which every outcome must be decided, while nothing sets which way it goes.

facts.t: Until an outcome is decided it stays open; once decided it stays decided, and each decision opens new undecided things.
Determination stands between the two pairs of Axioms.
The Determination fragment has eleven pieces, none found.

nodes.label: The Axiom strain
nodes.summary: The ripple from a strained Axiom, spreading slowly through the planes as Monoliths form more often.

facts.t: Over the past century Monoliths have formed more often, partly by Vecna's doing and partly because worlds reached their moments.
The rise strains an Axiom, and the strain ripples outward through the planes and the cosmos, weakening as it travels.
Mortals are starting to feel the strain: Gregory's awakening, the Latchling and other oddities are its results.
The ripple woke Astra Virex and caused collisions between celestial bodies.
The strain helps Vecna, Tharizdun and other powers, good and bad.

nodes.label: Paracausality
nodes.summary: A thing whose place in the structure of reality has been altered.

facts.t: A paracausal thing has had how it exists changed, along one particular axis.
Paracausality and the Weave are separate axes.
Paracausal beings often develop a resonance, a sense of other paracausal events nearby.

nodes.label: Polarity
nodes.summary: Why gods cannot walk on worlds or reach the center.

facts.t: Gods are of the same make as worlds and their hearts, so like charges push them apart, harder the closer they come.
The greater a god, the harder the push, which is why the greatest gods are kept farthest from worlds and the center.
The center harms gods without destroying them.
Polarity is why gods act through champions and vessels.

nodes.label: The Reach
nodes.summary: The act of the people of the first world, who reached into Continuity and changed it; their world was destroyed.

facts.t: The people of the first world, the only world in an earlier version of reality, reached into Continuity and changed it.
It was the first time Continuity had to answer, and the Core Monolith stands where it answered.
Most gods came into being in the Reach and grew into godhood over time.

nodes.label: The Reach world
nodes.summary: The first world, where the Reach happened; it collapsed into Rykoe.

facts.t: The Reach world was destroyed by the Reach, and its fragments spread across the cosmos as residue.
Its people became woven into the cosmos, and over time they became the gods.
Its people's own name for their world went into the Core Monolith with them.

nodes.label: Rykoe
nodes.summary: The center of the cosmos: the remains of the Reach world, a black hole beneath the Core Monolith.

facts.t: Rykoe is the remains of the Reach world, a black hole beneath the Core Monolith and the Radiant Citadel.
Rykoe opens only when the cores of all five galaxies are awake and joined.
Mortals can cross the approach; it harms gods without destroying them.
Rykoe is not a plane, so reaching it is travel rather than planar transit.

nodes.label: The Core Monolith
nodes.summary: The first Monolith, at the center of the cosmos; every Monolith relays to it.

facts.t: The Core manifested above the Reach world during its Zenith and remained after the world was destroyed.
Those who dwell in the Core Monolith call it Aurath.
Every other Monolith relays what it archives to the Core, and the Core's intake never closes.
The Core Monolith has a degree of sentience and presses an idea outward through the cosmos.
The presence in the Core has never issued a directive; the Order reads it as the All-Father and the Restorers as the All-Mother.
The Core is not public knowledge, and most gods do not understand it.

nodes.label: The Radiant Citadel
nodes.summary: The city the archived built inside the Core.

facts.t: The Citadel holds everything the Monoliths have ever taken, beginning with the people of the Reach world.
It presents as a golden age and is stratified underneath by order of arrival.
Time in the Citadel wears away memory of the outside world.
Nothing has ever come out of the Citadel, and a sect of the recently taken wants a way out.

nodes.label: Vecna (Lich)
nodes.summary: Vecna's mortal form, archived by Oerth's Monolith when he became a god.

facts.t: Vecna (Lich) is the mortal form Oerth's Monolith archived when Vecna ascended and relayed to the Core Monolith; he sits in the Radiant Citadel.
He has had centuries to conclude he was wrong, and he is calm, almost redeemed.
He holds the shape of Vecna's ambition and none of its method.
He is a separate character from Vecna, with his own dossier.

nodes.label: The First Heart
nodes.summary: The Reach world's heart, the deepest in the cosmos, beneath Rykoe; closed since the Reach.

facts.t: The First Heart lies beneath Rykoe, and every other heart pulls faintly toward it.
It has been closed since the Reach world ended.
Vecna knows the First Heart exists; the Restorers and the colony do not.

nodes.label: The Yearning
nodes.summary: The pull every child heart holds toward the First Heart.

facts.t: Before there were worlds there was one thing, and the separation left a pull in each world's heart.
The Yearning is why a world does not resist being joined to another.

nodes.label: Hearts
nodes.summary: Every world's metaphysical interior, the thinnest point between a world and the Axioms.

facts.t: Every world has a heart, its accumulated self, and a heart persists after its world is destroyed.
Finding a heart, opening it and linking it are three separate, hard steps.
Many worlds have a Monolith, far fewer a found heart, fewer an opened one, and only a couple are linked.
Two linked hearts form a permanent two-way passage, and linked worlds bleed into each other.

nodes.label: Atria
nodes.summary: The hidden entrance every heart has.

facts.t: Every heart has an Atrium, its own hidden entrance, which manifests differently on each world.
Residue carried into an Atrium opens the heart, and opening needs no Monolith.
The descent past an Atrium is made of what the world is.

nodes.label: Monoliths
nodes.summary: Continuity's response to a Zenith that strains it past tolerance.

facts.t: A Monolith archives a world bodily before an irreversible change and relays what it takes to the Core.
A Monolith is what makes a heart-link possible: two opened hearts link only where both worlds have one.
A Monolith belongs to no one and serves nothing beyond preservation.
A god standing in a dying world is not taken, because it is not about to cease.
The Order calls a Monolith an Ortholith in its records.

nodes.label: Zeniths
nodes.summary: The moment a world or people crosses into an irreversible change.

facts.t: A Zenith is a hinge rather than a disaster, and its outcome is unknown while it happens.
Zeniths are natural and constant, and mortals seeking power produce the most unstable ones.
Zeniths are arriving more often than the Order can explain.

nodes.label: Residue
nodes.summary: The pieces of the Reach fragments: Reach world matter, paracausal by origin.

facts.t: Residue is the only matter that can act on an Atrium, and a piece is not consumed by opening one.
The five fragments broke by Axiom into prime numbers of pieces: Dissolution 2, Distinction 3, Expansion 5, Consolidation 7, Determination 11.
Pieces of one fragment draw toward each other; pieces of different fragments are indifferent.
The Erevos Galaxy holds pieces of three fragments, Consolidation, Dissolution and Distinction, by chance and by pull.
Every enchanted thing carries a trace of residue.
Pieces are scarce, and every piece is a race.

nodes.label: The Circle of Fifths
nodes.summary: Vecna's name for his working: five galaxies, each a fifth of what he needs, around Rykoe. GAL-01's fifth is the eye inscription.

facts.t: He named it after the circle of fifths in music: five galaxies, each a fifth of what he needs, around Rykoe. The name is his alone.
In GAL-01 the working is the eye inscription: fifteen heart worlds, ten on the lids and five in the iris, which line up into an eye only as seen from Oerth.
Oerth is not one of the fifteen; every heart world in the figure links back to Oerth's heart.
Three of the fifteen hearts are found and two opened and linked, each also linked to Oerth; Nowhere's heart is found and not opened.
Only Vecna knows what he is building; the Seekers and the Order do not.

nodes.label: The Erevos Galaxy (GAL-01)
nodes.summary: Caelestis's galaxy, home to Realmspace, Fonains and Krynn.

facts.t: The Erevos Galaxy is named for Erevos, the black hole at its core: the pupil of Vecna's eye.
GAL-01 runs as D&D 5e.
It holds pieces of three residue fragments.
Its elemental planes are where the Princes of Elemental Evil work.
Caelestis and its affiliates chart this galaxy and know almost nothing of the others.

nodes.label: GAL-02
nodes.summary: The galaxy of the eldritch gods.

facts.t: GAL-02 has gods, none of them good; its gods are eldritch and gathered there over time.
No prime or good god holds GAL-02, and it has no Weave.
GAL-02 runs as Call of Cthulhu.
GAL-02's core is already awake, and the galaxy is overrun by dark beings.

nodes.label: The Astral Sea
nodes.summary: The material medium between worlds, systems and galaxies.

facts.t: The Astral Sea fills the dark between systems and between galaxies; the Fleet calls it the drift.
The corpses of gods drift through it, worked by salvagers, hermits and githyanki.
Color pools open and close quickly; the Fleet charts them and sails around them.
Most bodies in space are uninhabited, and an inhabited world is rare.

nodes.label: Color pools
nodes.summary: Portals adrift in the Astral Sea, each opening onto another plane.

facts.t: Color pools open and close quickly, and each opens onto another plane.
The Fleet charts color pools and sails around them.

nodes.label: Nowhere
nodes.summary: A world destroyed when a lesser god forced its way onto it; a lid world of Vecna's eye, its heart exposed.

facts.t: A lesser god forced its way into a system and down onto a world; the push destroyed them both.
A Monolith answered the destruction.
Its heart lies exposed in the wreck, found and not yet opened: a lid world of GAL-01's eye.
Every god since has taken it as a warning.

nodes.label: Vecna (Deity)
nodes.summary: God of secrets, knowledge, manipulation and trickery, working to wake the Erevos Galaxy's core and reach Continuity.

facts.t: Vecna is a later god who ascended on Oerth, his homeworld, at least a few centuries ago.
His domains are Knowledge, Death and Trickery, and his symbol is an eye in the palm of a left hand.
He keeps his name and origin a close secret, and most of his worshippers know him by other names.
He wants to understand the cosmos and become part of it: where everything came from, what the Reach was, what was taken from him.
Ascension charged him to Oerth's heart and pushed him off the world, so he works through vessels.
His realm is Cavitius.
He believes he could repair whatever breaks, and breaking reality is not his goal.
Only on Oerth is he worshipped openly as Vecna; elsewhere his faithful call him by other names, the First Seeker among them.

nodes.label: The Godhood Ascension
nodes.summary: Vecna's first ascension, on Oerth.

facts.t: Vecna's ritual pushed Oerth to its Zenith, and the Zenith made him a god.
The Monolith that answered archived his mortal form, Vecna (Lich).
A few centuries ago the gods of the Accordance felt a new entity like them appear where there had been none.

nodes.label: The Axiomic Ascension
nodes.summary: Vecna's climb now under way, to take an Axiom's place.

facts.t: The Ascension still to come is Vecna's climb to Axiom.
N'ghathrod is a means to an end: Vecna needs him to open and link hearts so his vessels can pass through Atria.
Getting N'ghathrod's five lieutenants through would make the working certain.
Many lesser taken, grown through the colony's spread, could still get him there.
A confrontation with Vecna could be with a part of him manifested in the First Heart.

nodes.label: Oerth
nodes.summary: Vecna's homeworld in Greyspace, where he became a god: the Ascension World.

facts.t: Oerth is a darkest-timeline world where Vecna's hold is strongest.
Oerth's Monolith is a holy site of Vecna's faith.
On Oerth his worship is large and public.
Oerth lies in Greyspace, in GAL-01, the Erevos Galaxy.
Oerth is the retina of the eye drawn across GAL-01: every heart world in the figure links back to it.
Oerth is the one world Vecna cannot lose.
Oerth's Monolith archived Vecna's mortal form, Vecna (Lich), and relayed it to the Core Monolith.

nodes.label: Cavitius
nodes.summary: Vecna's realm.

facts.t: Cavitius is Vecna's realm.

nodes.label: Tharizdun
nodes.summary: The imprisoned god of entropy, the Elder Elemental Eye.

facts.t: Tharizdun is sealed in a prison with no address in any known cosmology.
The purple slit-pupiled eye seen in the year 425 is the Elder Elemental Eye, Tharizdun.
Tharizdun is not lucid; she is an opportunist.
Fonains's Monolith is the only one ever to carry Tharizdun's crystal.
Tharizdun wanted nothing from Thessalar but chaos.
Her weakening of reality on Fonains serves Vecna's ends.

nodes.label: Shothragot
nodes.summary: Tharizdun's avatar, bound to the temple aboard the planar craft.

facts.t: Shothragot was bound to Tharizdun's temple aboard Thessalar's planar craft.
Its true vestige may still lie in that fallen temple.

nodes.label: Asmodeus
nodes.summary: Lord of the Nine Hells, eldest god of the Accordance and its face.

facts.t: Asmodeus began as a good-natured god and took up the fight against the demons the Reach let loose.
He was betrayed and became lord of the Nine Hells.
He is called evil because someone has to do his work, and he does it.
Asmodeus is the face of the Accordance, though not its ruler or leader.
He likely knows something is wrong in the cosmos.

nodes.label: Lord Primus
nodes.summary: One of the two eldest gods of the Accordance.

facts.t: Lord Primus and Asmodeus are the eldest gods of the Accordance.
Lord Primus may sense the new god that appeared a few centuries ago.

nodes.label: The Accordance
nodes.summary: Six gods who sealed the Princes of Elemental Evil and act through champions.

facts.t: About twelve thousand years ago the six gods of the Accordance sealed the Princes away, with four forged weapons as the keys.
The Accordance know little of Vecna.
The Accordance sent Lola's Boys back to the year 425.
Its six gods are Lord Primus, Asmodeus, Eldath, Muriel, Ryujin and Futsunushi.
Its emissary is Nalsa, an androsphinx.
Asmodeus is its face, though not its ruler or leader; he and Lord Primus are its eldest.

nodes.label: Eldath
nodes.summary: A god of the Accordance, keeper of the Misty Vale's tree.

facts.t: Eldath is one of the six gods of the Accordance.
Aerisi split Eldath's tree in the Misty Vale to take the air spear.

nodes.label: Tymora
nodes.summary: Lady Luck, Beshaba's twin.

facts.t: Tymora is goddess of good fortune and Beshaba's twin.
On Aethris Tymora is the greater of the twins, because people favour luck over misfortune.
Tymora does not know that she and Beshaba need each other.

nodes.label: Beshaba
nodes.summary: Maid of Misfortune, Sol's patron.

facts.t: Beshaba finds the Fortuned heretical and blames Tymora for fuelling them.
Luck and misfortune are two sides of one coin, and neither twin knows they need each other.
Her reward for Sol's oath is power, shaped through a want of her own laid on him as a quest.
Beshaba did not arrange Sol's escape from Aethris.
Aethris invented the Misfortuned through Tymora's worship; Beshaba did nothing to that world.
Beshaba's reward for Sol's oath is power, given shape by a want she lays on him as a quest.
She is strongest on Aethris, where she is the lesser of the two sisters.

nodes.label: Astra Virex
nodes.summary: A wounded celestial body, calling people to it to heal and become whole.

facts.t: The Axiom strain's ripple woke Astra Virex and broke part of it off in a collision of celestial bodies.
All it knows is that it must heal and become whole.
It can be called Astra Virex, Astra or Virex.
Those who answer its call and are changed become Starchildren, and their presence extends it into the regions they live in.
It is oriented toward constellations and knows nothing of world-hearts.
It runs parallel to Vecna's working and has no part in it.
Its missions read as grief: disappearances and people changed.

nodes.label: Starchildren
nodes.summary: Those who answered Astra Virex's call and were changed by it.

facts.t: Every constellation point a Starchild attunes to becomes a tether that anchors Astra Virex into that region.
Where several Starchildren have tethered, the change accelerates and becomes loud enough to feel.

nodes.label: Takhisis
nodes.summary: The Dragon Queen, known elsewhere as Tiamat.

facts.t: Takhisis is Tiamat, one god under two names.
She works through her armies while still bound, and the War of the Lance has not begun.
She holds an aspect of Bahamut trapped in the ruined temple of Paladine.

nodes.label: Bahamut
nodes.summary: The platinum dragon, known on Krynn as Paladine.

facts.t: Paladine is Bahamut, one god under two names.
An aspect of Bahamut is trapped by Takhisis in the ruined temple of Paladine on Krynn.
The trapped aspect speaks through Eldree's egg on Fonains.

nodes.label: The Seekers
nodes.summary: Vecna's faith, in chapters each named for what it seeks.

facts.t: The Seekers are Vecna's faith, and seeking is the faith itself.
Every chapter worships Vecna, often under another name or believing he is something else.
Chapters do not know about each other, and their mutual ignorance is a secret Vecna feeds on.
Each chapter's name carries its people's word for seekers.
Vecna lets each chapter believe that residue artifacts will lead it to what it seeks.
Vecna plants one idea in every chapter: seek what you are missing, what you yearn for, what was taken from you.
Vecna gives the faithful knowledge, the means of seeking and power; his clerics and wizards draw on him.
Chapters mostly use the eye from his symbol, rarely the hand; green eye-slit gems, neck eye tattoos and black candles burning green are common marks.
Only on Oerth is he worshipped openly as Vecna; elsewhere his faithful use other names, the First Seeker among them.
Chapters spread by seeding, by travellers, across the planes and by being found in ruins.

nodes.label: The Seekers of Secrets
nodes.summary: One Seekers chapter, named for what it seeks.

facts.t: The Seekers of Secrets are one chapter of Vecna's faith.

nodes.label: The Fracture Cult
nodes.summary: A Seekers chapter that drives worlds to their Zenith.

facts.t: The Fracture Cult is a Seekers chapter that seeks to bring worlds to their Zenith.
It accelerates worlds toward Zenith through engineered crises and symbolic acts.

nodes.label: The Archivists
nodes.summary: A Seekers chapter that seeks what the Monoliths record.

facts.t: The Archivists are a Seekers chapter that seeks what the Monoliths record.
They are drawn to Monolith sites, incomplete archives and corrupted records.

nodes.label: The church of the hand and eye
nodes.summary: The first Seekers chapter the crew meets: a benevolent church that shows Vecna's hand and eye openly.

facts.t: It is a good and docile church that shows Vecna's hand and eye openly, with something a little odd about it.
The crew first hears of it through Hessa Dun, and meets it well after graduation.

nodes.label: Hessa Dun
nodes.summary: A third-intake cadet who posts a notice-board job, and whose uncle collects things and likes visitors.

facts.t: Hessa Dun is a third-intake cadet at the Academy, planted in Arc 1.
She posts a notice-board job: hands and a strong back wanted to move her family's crates.
She mentions that her uncle collects a lot of things and likes visitors.

nodes.label: Hessa Dun's uncle
nodes.summary: A collector who likes visitors; not openly a Seeker.

facts.t: He collects a lot of things and likes visitors.
He is not openly a Seeker.

nodes.label: The Order of the All-Father
nodes.summary: An interworld order that preserves Continuity and reads the Core's pressure as the All-Father.

facts.t: The Order made Galactic time cycles and calls the count the Hearth: a hearthfire (cycle) is one full turn of Erevos, its four kindlings lighting the arms in order, divided into embers and sparks; Cycle 0 is the Order's founding and the current cycle is 1491.
Over the past few centuries the arms have kindled slightly early and the hearthfires have grown slightly shorter, and Watchers record them as irregular.
The Order takes the Core Monolith's pressure as a charge to maintain things as they are, though some within it doubt that reading.
The Order guards Monoliths believing the taken are inside them, when everything taken goes to the Core.
The Order spans the galaxies and is more organized than Caelestis and its affiliates.
Its device is a white tower with a blue-violet eye, and its members' magic shows as violet light and cosmic dust.
Its leadership instructs in aphorisms, which juniors sometimes take as literal orders.

nodes.label: The Watchers
nodes.summary: The Order's sanctioned field arm.

facts.t: Over the past century the Watchers have seen Monoliths rise more often, and it worries them; some want to act.
They are fighting oddities across many worlds and trying to keep a lid on them.
They flag some Seekers chapters' work as a danger to a world's Zenith without knowing who stands behind it.
Trainees spend about a century in the Hall of Sight and Sound before they are knighted as Watchers.
The Watchers rely on the Fleet for transport and reach.

nodes.label: The Rogue Watchers
nodes.summary: Watchers who act on their own judgment outside the Order's protocols.

facts.t: Rogue Watchers range from near-sanctioned to openly heterodox, and most worlds cannot tell them from sanctioned Watchers.

nodes.label: The Hall of Sight and Sound
nodes.summary: The great hall within the Order's seat.

facts.t: The Hall of Sight and Sound is the great hall within the Order's seat.
Trainees are knighted and christened Watchers there.

nodes.label: Captain-Commander Dejexic
nodes.summary: Leader of the Watchers and speaker of the All-Father.

facts.t: Dejexic is a purplish-blue plasmoid in obsidian armour with galaxies swirling in its reflection.
He floats, barely raises his voice, and silences a hall by entering it.
He told Ezra at his knighting to watch the birds, and Ezra took it literally.

nodes.label: Ezra Ahl-Sier
nodes.summary: An astral elf Glimpse of the Order, travelling with a Caelestis crew to finish his training on H'Catha.

facts.t: Ezra is an astral elf paladin of the Oath of the Watchers near the end of about a century of training.
He goes to H'Catha to finish his field training under its Watcher, and stays there when the crew leaves.
Privately he once thought a suffering world might be better ended, and he has told no one.
His posting after knighthood is Emporia.
His Channel Divinity guards allies against being reached into.
Caelestis is his prequel; his knighting, his posting to Emporia and his allies come after the crew leaves him on H'Catha.
A Caelestis crew later carries him from H'Catha to the Hall, the last troop he travels with.

nodes.label: Nereth Vaul
nodes.summary: H'Catha's Watcher, posted at the rim fog.

facts.t: Nereth Vaul is H'Catha's Watcher.
She filed the report on the meteor strike that started the H'Catha dispute.
She is the instructor Ezra goes to H'Catha to meet.

nodes.label: Aurel Venn
nodes.summary: A Watcher who saw the pattern, was not heeded, and left his post to find it himself.

facts.t: Aurel Venn warned the Order about the rising traffic at the edges and was not heeded.
He never broke with the Order openly, but he left his post to find the thing himself.
The crew hears of him through contradictory accounts long before any meeting.

nodes.label: The Restorers
nodes.summary: An order of scholars working to recover what the cosmos has lost, aimed at the Core.

facts.t: The Restorers are trying to reach a heart, and through it the Core Monolith, where they believe everything lost is stored.
They take the Core's pressure as a call to bring back what was lost, and they read its presence as the All-Mother.
They compete for residue pieces and, without knowing it, advance Vecna's plan.
The Restorers and the Seekers are separate, and they have clashed over the years.
For four centuries Restorers have walked into Zeniths on purpose to be archived, and many arrived.
They work in cells of four to nine, and standing is measured in Readings from a First through a Fifth.
Four living Fifth Readings hold the work on the approach to the Core.
Their own name for their work is the Return.
As the Restorers understand it, restoring a world takes a Monolith, a heart and all five fragments of residue.
The Order and the Restorers treat each other as heretics; the Order calls them a death cult.

nodes.label: The Ledger
nodes.summary: The Restorers' record of established losses, held in deliberately partial copies.

facts.t: The Ledger is distributed across Restorer cells so that no one holds all of it.
The Fonains entry, a Monolith that stood and then did not, is the most studied item in the Ledger.

nodes.label: Ilsabet Crann
nodes.summary: A hadozee Restorer of the Third Reading, keeping a cell of six on a trade station.

facts.t: Ilsabet Crann holds a Ledger segment covering four decades of Realmspace losses.
She earned her Third Reading by establishing a lost settlement of eleven hundred people nobody had recorded.
The pattern of rising Zeniths already sits in her segment, read as history rather than as a sequence.
She trades honestly and says plainly that she is trading rather than helping.

nodes.label: Ilsevaine Corr
nodes.summary: Ruler of a hidden polity at the edge of a system, keeping watch for something large.

facts.t: Ilsevaine Corr rules a hidden polity at the edge of a system or between systems.
She has noticed more traffic than usual near her borders, and once something large brushed the edge of her sight.
She is the one who will one day face Vth'oramu.
Once N'ghathrod grows bolder, she will face Vth'oramu.

nodes.label: The sage of Ascher Mir
nodes.summary: A fringe sage who tracks the Seekers' pattern across chapters.

facts.t: The fringe sage of Ascher Mir tracks the Seekers' pattern across chapters.
The few on the fringes who sense something wrong in the cosmos are not believed.

nodes.label: The edge mystery
nodes.summary: Something at the edge, outside Realmspace, that will cross Vth'oramu's path.

facts.t: A mystery lies at the edge, outside Realmspace, in another system or between systems.
It will cross paths with Vth'oramu once N'ghathrod grows bolder.

nodes.label: The United Intergalactic Fleet
nodes.summary: Four sector branches, one on each arm of the Erevos Galaxy, under a council of admirals. Caelestis founded it and is one of its sectors.

facts.t: The Fleet is made of four sector branches, one along each of the Erevos Galaxy's four spiral arms, each overseeing a cluster of systems.
Caelestis founded the Fleet: it proposed a combined fleet, and the Caelestis Sector lies on Realmspace's arm.
The Fleet dates by Galactic time cycles (GTC), the Order's count, adopted when the Fleet formed about 250 cycles ago; the current cycle is 1491.
Not every spelljammer belongs to the Fleet; independents, other factions and smaller mercantile houses, Vocath's crew among them, work outside it.
Above the sectors sits a council of a few admirals, not a single leader.
The sectors began as separate institutions; each keeps its own ways and names, and they share information but not all of it.
The Fleet keeps a self-imposed order, and much of its work is mercantile: shipments, protection, passengers and transport for the Watchers.
The Fleet lost a force at Glyth, and Glyth is closed to Fleet traffic.

nodes.label: A.T.L.A.S.
nodes.summary: A brass-and-glass device housing a Distinction piece; it reveals the aspects of a world, its heart among them.

facts.t: A.T.L.A.S. houses one Distinction piece and reveals the aspects of a world, a world's heart among them.
It is held in the Brig at Caelestis, catalogued as an antique navigational instrument.
A reader sees as deep as their understanding allows: surface features, then a world's Atrium, then the Yearning and any live links.
As one of three Distinction pieces it pulls toward the other two.
Whoever first cut the piece out and built its housing is unrecorded.

nodes.label: Second Distinction piece
nodes.summary: A second Distinction housing; it seems to find magic items and truly finds Reach artifacts.

facts.t: The second Distinction piece is housed in a device, which Caelestis held.
On the surface it finds magic items; its true use is finding Reach artifacts.
Vocath's crew ambushed the Bellwether Crow to take it.
Clint carried it through the color pool, and it is somewhere on Fonains.

nodes.label: The third Distinction piece
nodes.summary: The last piece of the Distinction fragment, whereabouts unknown.

facts.t: The third Distinction piece finds something too.

nodes.label: The Distinction fragment
nodes.summary: Distinction residue, in three pieces.

facts.t: The Distinction fragment is in three pieces.
Every Distinction piece, in whatever housing, finds or reveals something: it tells one thing apart from everything else.

nodes.label: The Dissolution fragment
nodes.summary: The fragment the Runekeepers carry, two pieces, now forming in Wan and Tu.

facts.t: The Dissolution fragment lies in two pieces.
It cycles between whole and broken across Runekeepers, and its oscillation powers the concealment of the Wayfinders' homeworld.
In Tumak it is rebuilding in two halves at once, a three-part state.
The twins carry the Dissolution fragment.
It is visible in its bearers, forming and re-forming in the chest of the Runekeeper and of the Wayfinders who carry it.

nodes.label: The Expansion fragment
nodes.summary: Expansion residue, in five pieces, none located.

facts.t: The Expansion fragment is in five pieces, and none has been located; none lies in the Erevos Galaxy.

nodes.label: The Determination fragment
nodes.summary: Determination residue, in eleven pieces, none ever found.

facts.t: The Determination fragment is in eleven pieces, and none has ever been found; none lies in the Erevos Galaxy.

nodes.label: The Rod of Seven Parts
nodes.summary: The Consolidation fragment, seven pieces each known by its working.

facts.t: Each Rod piece performs a single working impossibly well, so a piece can be recognized by its effect.
A Consolidation piece feels the other six and a direction toward them.
Four of its pieces are loose and their workings unidentified.
Its pieces have yearned toward each other for ages, and several now sit near Realmspace.

nodes.label: The Rod's fifth piece
nodes.summary: A Consolidation piece keyed to find the path, held by Xanathar.

facts.t: The fifth Rod piece is keyed to find the path and is held by Xanathar.
It was Vaelorix's next target when he died.

nodes.label: The Rod's seventh piece
nodes.summary: The Consolidation piece keyed to simulacrum, held by Thessalar.

facts.t: The seventh Rod piece is keyed to simulacrum.
It is why N'ghathrod's tadpoles make copies of him, and it is the root of the taking.
Thessalar holds it.

nodes.label: Xanathar
nodes.summary: The holder of the Rod's fifth piece.

facts.t: Xanathar is a known quantity in a known city, which makes the fifth piece the most reachable unclaimed one.

nodes.label: The colony's residue piece
nodes.summary: The one residue piece on Vecna's side, carried by the colony from world to world.

facts.t: Vecna's side holds one residue piece, and the colony carries it from world to world to open hearts.
If it is taken, N'ghathrod must win it back or find another before he can open another heart.

nodes.label: N'ghathrod
nodes.summary: Founder of the Vth'orama, fused into Vth'oramu; the campaign's main villain.

facts.t: N'ghathrod is the main villain of the campaign, and Vecna stands behind him.
About five hundred years ago Thessalar captured him and experimented on him with the Rod's seventh piece.
His long life comes from his taken: a portion of each is tithed upward to him, and the more he takes, the longer he lasts.
He is not immortal.
If his true body dies the taken live on, each keeping part of him, and one could grow toward becoming another N'ghathrod.
He believes the voice that guides him is an elder brain; it is Vecna.
He was a spacefaring elf before ceremorphosis.
He is working on all four parts of his plan now: placing the taken, finding hearts, opening them and seeking links.
His join with Vth'oramu is permanent; only a wish or an artifact could break it.
His colony's mark is the eye in a wheel: ordinary spokes above, illithid tentacles below.
He knows the Order's Watchers exist, through the Watchers posted to Glyth.

nodes.label: N'ghathrod's mouse
nodes.summary: A mouse N'ghathrod saved in his escape, with him ever since.

facts.t: In the escape from the planar craft N'ghathrod saved a mouse, which has travelled with him since.
The mouse was in the same room as the Rod's seventh piece for as long as he was.

nodes.label: The Aspect
nodes.summary: A long-tenured taken, dominated and wrapped in illusion, who walks and speaks as N'ghathrod.

facts.t: The colony turns to the Aspect as N'ghathrod, and another appears within weeks wearing the same face if one dies.
The body in the chamber is a shell kept for the founders; his true body is fused into the hull.

nodes.label: N'ghathrod's elder brain
nodes.summary: The elder brain separated from N'ghathrod in the crash, buried for five centuries under the Barrier Peaks.

facts.t: N'ghathrod's elder brain was separated from him in the crash, and he believed it dead or could not reach it.
It lay trapped beneath the Barrier Peaks for about five hundred years, possibly growing a colony of its own.
Lola's Boys broke it in Session 27; it was buried in the collapse but teleported out and escaped.

nodes.label: The Vth'orama
nodes.summary: N'ghathrod's illithid colony, the Seekers of a New Home.

facts.t: The colony's mark is an eye inside a wheel: the top half has ordinary spokes and the bottom half turns into illithid tentacles; the wheel is navigation, finding a way home.
The colony is a chapter of the Seekers, the Seekers of a New Home, believing it answers to an elder brain.
Vth'orama means all who go toward home: vth- the whole of, or- toward, amu home, -a a people.
Vecna feeds the colony the few secrets it needs.
The colony's arms echo a hand and an eye without showing either outright.
When a taken person dies, N'ghathrod receives what it knew.
Tadpoles pay for everything the colony does, and a crate destroyed in transit costs months of placements.
Qualith is the only writing the colony counts as real.
The colony works on four things at once: planting the taken, finding hearts, opening them and seeking links.
Vth'oramu keeps to the dark between systems and works as a mothership for skiffs.
The colony takes key people who can rise into control, never crowds.

nodes.label: The taken
nodes.summary: Everyone implanted with N'ghathrod's tadpoles; the Vth'ghathu.

facts.t: Every taken person comes from N'ghathrod's tadpoles, which are copies of him.
As each taken grows, a portion passes up through the rungs and ends with N'ghathrod; the flow is paracausal.
A taken person keeps their memories and self, grows hidden chitin, and carries an innate mind blank.
The taken lose a part of themselves if N'ghathrod dies, but they do not die.
A taken person's faculties grow with tenure toward N'ghathrod's own.

nodes.label: The Enna Vth'ghathu
nodes.summary: N'ghathrod's five lieutenants, the near-held, each carrying a Hold of him.

facts.t: The five lieutenants were changed with N'ghathrod by Thessalar's experiments and gained greatly extended lifespans.
Two are properly raised illithids captured with N'ghathrod; three are unthinned, made aboard the craft from bodies Thessalar supplied and N'ghathrod's tadpoles.
Each carries a Hold, a portion of N'ghathrod, and he speaks through them at will.
Killing one ends that Hold, and the colony loses its function.
They are closest to N'ghathrod of all the taken.

nodes.label: The Vth'merru
nodes.summary: The bearers: properly raised illithids who can still breed the colony.

facts.t: The bearers lay into the pools and oversee ordinary ceremorphosis.
They watch bodies that should have become illithids receive N'ghathrod's tadpoles instead, and resent it as waste.
Osskhal and Khaleth, two of the enna, are bearers captured with N'ghathrod aboard Thessalar's craft.

nodes.label: The Vth'ulhan
nodes.summary: The unthinned: illithids raised without an elder brain to cull them.

facts.t: Glyth exiled the unthinned, and N'ghathrod went with them because they are his blood.
The unthinned took Glyth's insult for themselves.
They are the bulk of the colony's illithids and loyal for what N'ghathrod did for them.

nodes.label: Osskhal
nodes.summary: The Flesh: the enna who carries the body N'ghathrod fights with.

facts.t: Osskhal is properly raised and carries the Hold of the Flesh.
He is an unremarkable mind flayer who is better at violence than anything the crew has met.
He is the one who argues with N'ghathrod in front of others.
Properly raised and captured with N'ghathrod aboard Thessalar's craft; Thessalar's experiments gave him a greatly extended lifespan.

nodes.label: Ulh'rek
nodes.summary: The Arcane: the enna who carries the spellcasting and keeps the Qualith library.

facts.t: Ulh'rek is unthinned, nine feet tall and malformed, and carries the Hold of the Arcane.
He keeps the colony's Qualith library, its charts and its research into Atria.
He is the best source in the cosmos on where Atria are.
Unthinned and made aboard Thessalar's craft; Thessalar's experiments gave him a greatly extended lifespan.

nodes.label: Zhauveth
nodes.summary: The Voice: the enna who carries domination and suggestion and makes the colony's arrangements.

facts.t: Zhauveth is unthinned, barely four feet tall, and incapable of violence.
She made the arrangement with Vocath about a year before the crew's first voyage.
Joffrey is her instrument on Caelestis.
People who meet her remember the conversation fondly and cannot reconstruct what was said.
Unthinned and made aboard Thessalar's craft; Thessalar's experiments gave her a greatly extended lifespan.

nodes.label: Ith'varn
nodes.summary: The Sight: the blind enna through whom every taken's report passes.

facts.t: Ith'varn is unthinned and blind, and reads the world through the colony bond.
Every taken person's reporting passes through him before it reaches N'ghathrod.
He has not left Vth'oramu in thirty years.
Unthinned and made aboard Thessalar's craft; Thessalar's experiments gave him a greatly extended lifespan.

nodes.label: Khaleth
nodes.summary: The Surveyor: the enna who runs the hunt for Atria and leads the descents.

facts.t: Khaleth is properly raised and carries the Hold of the Surveyor.
He is the only one of the five who goes down into a world's interior.
Of the five he is the most likely to leave a fight rather than finish it.
Properly raised and captured with N'ghathrod aboard Thessalar's craft; Thessalar's experiments gave him a greatly extended lifespan.

nodes.label: Vth'oramu
nodes.summary: A living astral dreadnought taken by N'ghathrod: ship, creature and home of the colony.

facts.t: Vth'oramu means the passage to a new home; the founders say it as a promise, and those born aboard say it as here.
The dreadnought bore no wound before the siege; a whisper from Vecna told N'ghathrod it was the best way to keep a colony on its passage home.
Taking it took decades, perhaps a century, and a great many tadpoles; generations were born aboard.
It keeps to the dark between systems as a mothership, sending skiffs to the worlds around it.
Its tether is an astral cord, a silver line running off to somewhere unknown, and its tail is immensely long.
Its great weapon is a pulse from its whole body that teleports away everything in range, slow to charge and rarely used.
N'ghathrod is fused into it, and most of the colony does not know they live inside him.
Its mouth draws things in to the demiplane its interior was widened into.
Its eye is the bridge; its mouth is the only way in, onto a demiplane crossed by fixed plane-shift transit points.
The earliest copies of N'ghathrod are in the dreadnought's walls.
Illithid arcanists from N'ghathrod's own crew keep its plane-shift transit points.

nodes.label: Glyth
nodes.summary: The illithid world in Realmspace that exiled the unthinned.

facts.t: The journey back to Glyth from the planar craft took decades.
Glyth exiled the unthinned roughly four to four and a half centuries ago.
Glyth is a settled illithid world with elder brains and thrall populations.
Glyth is hard to reach, on a long orbit with a rare approach window, and closed to Fleet traffic.

nodes.label: The exile from Glyth
nodes.summary: Glyth casts out the unthinned, and N'ghathrod leaves with them.

facts.t: Roughly four centuries ago Glyth rejected the unthinned and N'ghathrod chose to go with them.
In the centuries after, he searched for a home, learned the full reach of his taking, and Vecna began whispering to him.
The active push to find and open hearts began only in the past few decades.

nodes.label: Vocath
nodes.summary: A mercane merchant running a grudge against Mirt, and the unknowing tool of the colony.

facts.t: Vocath aims to disgrace Mirt enough to prise him loose from the school's protection so someone else can finish him.
He believes Joffrey answers to him; Joffrey is N'ghathrod's.
His trade line has been moving colony material for years.
Joffrey steered him to the Brig, and he experiences the plan as his own.
His mark is a private house mark: a balance scale, coins against cargo.
He used the Fleet's thinning to put stress on the Academy.
His price to N'ghathrod's side was captives from a Caelestis crew, read as ordinary thrall work.
He sees the Fleet stretched thin and uses it to press the Academy.

nodes.label: Vocath's crew
nodes.summary: A mercane trading house running a private grudge against Mirt, with a second principal it knows nothing of.

facts.t: The thefts, the sabotage plates, the leverage on Miken and the marked crates at the Sky Dock are Vocath's work.
Vocath's crew took Cairn Station after it went dark and waited for the relief run.
Vocath's crew ambushed the Bellwether Crow for the second Distinction piece.
Vocath's people chased Clint to Fonains, never found him, and came back with fragments of the broken Monolith.
Someone from Vocath's crew followed Clint to Fonains, learned about the gems there, and Vocath now trades in them.
Qitru serves Vocath and does not care who stands above him.

nodes.label: Vocath's house mark
nodes.summary: Vocath's private house mark.

facts.t: Vocath's house mark is a balance scale with coins on one pan and cargo on the other; it is his own merchant mark, so the Fleet registry has no entry for it.
The crates at the Sky Dock carry it.
The same sigil marks the sabotage plates in the Simulation Deck and the brand beneath the neogi's chitin.
Anyone who trades in the right circles reads it on sight.

nodes.label: Qitru
nodes.summary: A githyanki intermediary of Vocath's crew, following the crew by Miken's beacon.

facts.t: Qitru serves Vocath and does not care who stands above him.
She works from a star lancer and recruits, pays and collects for the operation.
She finds the crew through a beacon Miken planted aboard their ship.
Miken's report that the crew killed a beholder has reached her.
She pursues Vocath's aim, to make the cadet mission fail; Miken is her channel.

nodes.label: Joffrey
nodes.summary: A decorated Fleet officer, taken by the colony; its only operative on Caelestis.

facts.t: Joffrey was taken in the second boarding of the Bellwether Crow, the colony's backup to Vocath's ambush, by one of N'ghathrod's tadpoles.
The few survivors were let go so that he would come home a hero, and they believe every word of their account.
He is the colony's only operative on the station, and his allegiance runs to N'ghathrod.
His reports to Vocath have never contained a lie; he withholds only that A.T.L.A.S. is the point.
He found the Brig and told Vocath it was there.
He means to take A.T.L.A.S. from the Brig under cover of the graduation chaos.
He was top of his class and is named the present-day great spelljammer of Caelestis.
He was taken slowly: for months he was himself, and he finished converting only recently.
One survivor of the Crow noticed he had changed and never reported it.

nodes.label: Jeffrey
nodes.summary: A Sky Dock hand bribed to let manifests go unchecked.

facts.t: Jeffrey is a Sky Dock hand and Joffrey's friend, paid to let certain manifests go unchecked and crates move at odd hours.
He was bribed rather than taken, and believes he is helping a friend smuggle.
He has begun to suspect the money is too large for the work.

nodes.label: Bellwether Crow
nodes.summary: A Caelestis light corvette, the relief vessel ambushed on the Cairn approach a year ago.

facts.t: Bellwether Crow was sent to learn why Cairn Station had stopped answering.
It was carrying the second Distinction piece when Vocath's crew ambushed it.
A second boarding, by a different party, killed the senior deck officers and most of the complement.
Its survivors still argue about whether Clint meant to go through the color pool.
The Crow made Strake under damage.

nodes.label: Bellwether Crow ambush
nodes.summary: About a year before now, near Cairn Station: Joffrey taken, Clint gone overboard.

facts.t: About a year before now Vocath's crew ambushed the Bellwether Crow near Cairn Station.
Clint took the second Distinction piece and left the ship in one of the boarders' craft to draw them off.
Some of the boarders went after him and some stayed, and enough went that the crew fended off the rest.
The second action was N'ghathrod's colony, shadowing Vocath's ambush as a backup; with the device gone, it took Joffrey instead.
In the Fleet, a crew member who leaves the ship, willingly or not, and does not come back has gone overboard.

nodes.label: Clint Dashforest
nodes.summary: A Caelestis crewmate of the Bellwether Crow who went through a color pool and landed on Fonains.

facts.t: Clint took the second Distinction piece and left the Crow in one of the boarders' craft to draw them off.
He steered for a color pool he saw opening and went through it on purpose.
The pool carried him through a pocket of another dimension and spat him out on Fonains, apart from the boarders who followed.
He reached Fonains before its Monolith appeared.
He works as a bounty hunter out of Orerius, with a crew called the Six Shooters.
His laser pistol is the only piece of Caelestis on Fonains.
Saerthe and Tarto have worn a matched pair of bands of the lost and found since he was lost.
He landed about a year before the present and was on Fonains when its Monolith appeared.
On the Blooming Glass job his crew freed Chloe Chespetes and handed the Pedra Ardente to Finerva.

nodes.label: Miken Haverstance
nodes.summary: A cadet friend of the crew, leveraged by Vocath's crew; he does not flip.

facts.t: A mercane recruited Miken by paying his fiancé's debts.
He planted a beacon aboard the crew's ship so Qitru could follow them.
His sending-stone report told Vocath's people that the crew killed a beholder.
He is wrestling with guilt rather than hiding malice.
Miken stays leveraged and complicit, does not flip, and lives.
The moneylender behind the Tallow Wren contract holds his fiancé's debts.

nodes.label: The Brig
nodes.summary: Caelestis's Bay of Restricted Inert Goods, where A.T.L.A.S. is held.

facts.t: The Brig holds objects whose cosmological character is unknown, unstable or inconvenient to discuss.
Its location and access routes are classified, and teleportation fails in and out of it.
Only a handful at Bridge level know its full inventory.

nodes.label: The perimeter watch
nodes.summary: Strake Station and its sister satellites, Hollis Post and Cairn Station, watching the edge of Realmspace for the Caelestis Sector.

facts.t: The Caelestis Sector watches the edge of Realmspace from Strake Station and its two sister satellites, Hollis Post and Cairn Station.
Strake stands on the bearing called the Tetherbreak; everything past it is closed without Bridge authorization.

nodes.label: Strake Station
nodes.summary: The Caelestis Sector's waystation at the edge of Realmspace, with a small Fleet presence watching the edge; the last open deck before the closed run to Cairn.

facts.t: Strake Station and its sister satellites are Caelestis's to keep.
Strake Station reported an unidentified mass, and it was Vth'oramu.
Readings from the edge stations pass between the institutions.
An item is held in its secure storage under Quartermaster Verrow's seal.

nodes.label: Cairn Station
nodes.summary: The far satellite of the watch at Realmspace's edge, silent for a year.

facts.t: A year ago Vth'oramu sat on the Cairn bearing.
Cairn went silent after reporting a mass that matched no vessel profile.
Vocath's people withdrew after the ambush and left something behind at Cairn.

nodes.label: Hollis Post
nodes.summary: The western satellite of the watch at Realmspace's edge, filing normally.

facts.t: Hollis Post does the same job as Strake and Cairn, and nothing has happened to it.

nodes.label: M. Tarroway
nodes.summary: A cartographer on Strake Station whose readings first hinted at something at the edge.

facts.t: Tarroway's readings were the first hint that an unknown vessel or structure was disturbing the satellites at the edge of the system.
His name turns up here and there, mainly in the Fleet Intelligence Archive.
Nothing about him is public.

nodes.label: Quartermaster Halix Verrow
nodes.summary: Strake's quartermaster, who counter-signs everything that moves on the edge run to Cairn.

facts.t: Verrow enforces the standing order closing the run past Strake.
Whatever he signs, he stands behind.
He cannot be charmed, and lying to him makes an enemy who keeps records.

nodes.label: Fleet Intelligence Archive
nodes.summary: Caelestis's restricted intelligence record.

facts.t: The archive records the Cairn silence and the Crow's ambush and connects neither.

nodes.label: Caelestis Academy
nodes.summary: The Caelestis Spelljammer Academy: the school of the Caelestis Sector, which trains cadets to become Driftwardens.

facts.t: The Caelestis Spelljammer Academy trains cadets to become Driftwardens; there are only a handful of spelljammer academies in the galaxy.
Mirt runs the Academy only; the Corps and the Bridge operate outside him.
Caelestis is thin partly because it answers the Watchers' calls for help.
More Zeniths, more Watcher requests and movements at the galaxy's edge are straining the Fleet.
Its surveyors keep the Caelestis Survey Catalogue, which gives every charted star a number.

nodes.label: The Caelestis Corps
nodes.summary: The Caelestis Sector's branch of the Fleet. It oversees the sector; its operations run out of Ondrel Anchorage.

facts.t: The Caelestis Corps is the Caelestis Sector's branch of the Fleet and oversees the sector.
Fleet operations for the Caelestis Sector run out of Ondrel Anchorage, on the moon Ostrel.
Contracts surface because of the state of the world, and many quietly lead back to a Seekers chapter.
By the crew's graduation the colony's work ripples outward at contract scale: taken in small positions, disappearances, a station acting strangely.

nodes.label: Ondrel Anchorage
nodes.summary: A neutral port on the moon Ostrel, in a system neighbouring Realmspace within the Caelestis Sector.

facts.t: Ondrel Anchorage is a neutral port on the moon Ostrel, away from Toril.
Fleet operations for the Caelestis Sector run out of Ondrel Anchorage.

nodes.label: Captain Haymond Rolt
nodes.summary: The crew's handler in Arc 2, overseeing several Driftwarden crews from Ondrel Anchorage.

facts.t: Captain Haymond Rolt oversees several Driftwarden crews at once, out of Ondrel Anchorage.
He is an homage to Captain Raymond Holt; his look, manner and history are not set.

nodes.label: Caelestis
nodes.summary: The Fleet station in Toril orbit, home of the Academy.

facts.t: Caelestis is under permanent Forbiddance, maintained by Saerthe.
Authorized internal transit uses bound Teleportation Circle sigils between a few fixed points, the Brig among them.
Caelestis has no echo in the Feywild or the Shadowfell.
The thefts, the sabotage and Vocath's grudge are noise over one objective: A.T.L.A.S. in the Brig.

nodes.label: Mirt
nodes.summary: Headmaster of Caelestis Academy, in a long feud with Vocath.

facts.t: Mirt knows the house mark is Vocath's and cannot prove it in a filing.
He backed the closure of the run past Strake so nobody else would die there while he handles Vocath his own way.
The closure is how Joffrey walked onto his station unexamined.
He does not know his wardrobe is one of Zerathis's tethers.
Mirt runs the Academy only; the Caelestis Corps and the Bridge operate outside him.
Caelestis protects him and keeps him quiet, so he is also stuck there.

nodes.label: Boatswain Tarto
nodes.summary: A scarred hadozee instructor who runs the Simulation Deck.

facts.t: Tarto passed on the crate holding the neogi hatchlings because she was informed rather than having checked it herself.
She wants the name of whoever routed the neogi crate through her.
She had the helm once and gave it up.
One wing flap was torn away long ago, and she has not glided since.
She has four superiority dice, regained on a short rest.
When the CRC comes for Sol, she stands up for him.

nodes.label: Saerthe Abizjn
nodes.summary: Helm instructor and senior caster, keeper of the station's Forbiddance.

facts.t: Saerthe maintains Caelestis's Forbiddance and the registry of bound Teleportation Circle sigils.
He can mentally call a fleet of tethered spelljamming ships, at the cost of prolonged helm-blindness.
His quicksilver eyes are an origin trait tied to Nimbral.
Half of his missing miniature ship is inside Boogie.
He was not aboard the Bellwether Crow when Clint went overboard, and carries the guilt of it.

nodes.label: Sor'Kur
nodes.summary: The telepathic thri-kreen administrator.

facts.t: The access record that shows Joffrey's route to the Brig runs through Sor'Kur's desk.
Sor'Kur is one of two thri-kreen near the crew, and Ostekk's clockwork horrors speak thri-kreen.

nodes.label: Winston Ryeback
nodes.summary: Giff petty officer and galley cook of the Weeping Goddess.

facts.t: Ryeback's report to Caelestis says the crew killed the beholder.
He wants the cadets fed and alive, and treats both as the same job.
The Academy thefts took his custom pistol; the hand cannon is his own gun.
Ryeback lives; no death is planned for him.

nodes.label: Rindle Gearloft
nodes.summary: A rock gnome at the Sea Dock, hiding the Latchling.

facts.t: Rindle is hiding the Latchling at the Sea Dock and protecting it from the academy.
He believes the academy would take the Latchling apart.
The Latchling goes to Gregory as something familiar, and that reaction cracks Rindle's secrecy.

nodes.label: Mr. Blip
nodes.summary: The autognome who runs Stores.

facts.t: Mr. Blip is an autognome with ordinary personhood who cannot cast.
He is uninvolved in the run on the Brig.

nodes.label: Krik'Lit
nodes.summary: A thri-kreen deckhand, the one translator for Ostekk's machines.

facts.t: Krik'Lit translated the crew's parley with Ostekk-10, because Ostekk's clockwork horrors speak thri-kreen.
He and Pffred are relieved at the V006 swap and leave aboard the Flighty Foundling.

nodes.label: Veena
nodes.summary: A rival cadet, unconscious since the simulation blast.

facts.t: Veena and Derek have been unconscious since the blast in the simulation chamber, and nobody has asked why.

nodes.label: Derek
nodes.summary: A rival cadet, unconscious since the simulation blast.

facts.t: Derek has lain unconscious beside Veena since the blast, with no change recorded.

nodes.label: Captain Sardax
nodes.summary: Captain of the Moonraider, whose last fight the Academy keeps as a simulation.

facts.t: The Academy teaches Sardax as courage first and judgement second.
A simulation that detailed needed a source, and the record does not say what it was.

nodes.label: Simulation Deck
nodes.summary: Where the Trial by Fire simulations run.

facts.t: The sabotage on the Simulation Deck left metallic plates and a jagged sigil in the chamber walls.

nodes.label: Sky Dock
nodes.summary: The surface-facing dock.

facts.t: The bribed seam in the station's inventory handling is at the Sky Dock.
Colony material moves in and out of Caelestis through the Sky Dock.

nodes.label: The Sea Dock
nodes.summary: The lower cargo dock.

facts.t: The Latchling hides at the Sea Dock.

nodes.label: The Latchling
nodes.summary: A latch that became a self, hidden at the Sea Dock.

facts.t: The Latchling is a latch that gained sentience where its kind has none.
It is one result of the Axiom strain.
Gregory's repair of a latch may have been the local condition that let it wake.

nodes.label: Crated Centipede Creature
nodes.summary: A neogi hatchling from the crate delivered to Mirt.

facts.t: The creatures in the crate were neogi hatchlings, bound by an outside hand.
Sigils etched beneath the neogi's chitin match the sabotage plates.

nodes.label: Marked Crate at the Sky Dock
nodes.summary: A crate bearing Vocath's mark.

facts.t: The crates at the Sky Dock carry Vocath's house mark.

nodes.label: Vocath Arcane Rod
nodes.summary: The spent rod from the simulation chamber.

facts.t: The rod carries Vocath's house mark.

nodes.label: Moonraider
nodes.summary: Sardax's ship, lost to astral reavers.

facts.t: The Moonraider was boarded by astral reavers from a pirate galleon.

nodes.label: Derelict
nodes.summary: The wreck of the salvage exercise.

facts.t: The logbook came out of the simulation as a real object.

nodes.label: Derelict Logbook
nodes.summary: The logbook of the salvage exercise.

facts.t: Boogie holds half of the derelict logbook.
The other half was in his chest inside the Monolith.
The original logbook exists somewhere in Caelestis with pages missing.

nodes.label: Incomplete Model Spelljamming Ship
nodes.summary: The half-ship inside Boogie.

facts.t: The Fonains shard is what keeps the half-ship inside Boogie.

nodes.label: Saerthe's Miniature Spelljamming Ship
nodes.summary: Saerthe's missing miniature.

facts.t: Half of Saerthe's miniature ship is inside Boogie.

nodes.label: Miken's Sending Stone
nodes.summary: Miken's channel to Vocath's people.

facts.t: Miken made his report to Vocath's people through the sending stone.

nodes.label: Tyrant Ship
nodes.summary: Vaelorix's carved-stone beholder ship, now the crew's.

facts.t: Every beholder ship is carved stone, so a tyrant ship draws less concern at H'Catha's borders than an ordinary spelljammer.
Nobody on H'Catha knows Vaelorix is dead.

nodes.label: Vaelorix
nodes.summary: The Cultivant: a landless H'Cathan beholder who collected living things.

facts.t: Vaelorix stole the Containment Engine from Ostekk.
He pointed the Engine's regenerative working at a wisp-lotus symbiosis and got a paracausal eruption that killed him.
His next target was the Rod's fifth piece, held by Xanathar.
Something between him and Kurrzot was left unsettled.

nodes.label: Ostekk
nodes.summary: A ruling beholder of H'Catha and a builder, who made the Containment Engine and the OSTEKK units.

facts.t: Ostekk built the Containment Engine around the Rod's fourth piece without knowing it was Reach residue.
He built the OSTEKK units to depend on the Engine for their maintenance, securing loyalty through need.
He now has reason to come for the Engine himself: the crew took it and lied to his machine.
He rules one of H'Catha's ten domains like a workshop; he wants his property back.

nodes.label: Ostekk-6
nodes.summary: An OSTEKK automaton travelling with the crew.

facts.t: Ostekk-6 is the only active survivor of the nine OSTEKK units.
He was built with a fragment of the Lantern, which is why the Command Deck's field slowed him without stopping him.
He does not know that what keeps him running and what the behir sought are the same object.

nodes.label: Ostekk-2
nodes.summary: An OSTEKK automaton lying inert on the Hollow Deck.

facts.t: Ostekk-2 lies inert on the Hollow Deck.
The crew could heal Ostekk-2 back to function with the Lantern of Flourishing.

nodes.label: Ostekk-10
nodes.summary: Ostekk's clockwork behir.

facts.t: Ostekk built Ostekk-10 after the Engine and the nine units were stolen, to retrieve them.

nodes.label: The clockwork horrors
nodes.summary: Ostekk's constructs aboard the tyrant ship.

facts.t: The clockwork horrors were built by Ostekk and speak thri-kreen.
Their cores are resonance-attuned crystal from the same supply line behind other incidents.

nodes.label: Lantern of Flourishing
nodes.summary: The Containment Engine, Fourth Series: Ostekk's housing around the Rod's fourth piece.

facts.t: The crew carries the Rod's fourth piece, keyed to regenerate, in the Lantern.
The piece is extractable, and the Engine is not built to survive losing it.
Its name records three earlier attempts.
Its source is sealed inside the lamp, below the light, where identify cannot read.

nodes.label: The Command Deck
nodes.summary: The tyrant ship's helm deck.

facts.t: The Command Deck's field froze the clockwork horrors, slowed the OSTEKK units and kept the behir out.

nodes.label: The Hollow Deck
nodes.summary: The tyrant ship's repair deck.

facts.t: The Lantern's empty seat is above the repair-bay pod on the Hollow Deck.

nodes.label: The Garden
nodes.summary: Vaelorix's specimen garden.

facts.t: The garden holds Vaelorix's research specimens, including the bloom that woke Bartholomew's Aspects.

nodes.label: Garden Bloom
nodes.summary: The flower that woke Bartholomew's Aspects.

facts.t: The bloom is an accelerant for Bartholomew's Almost, not its key.

nodes.label: Faelight spore
nodes.summary: A fungus from Vaelorix's collection that throws a cloud of faerie light when fed a spell slot.

facts.t: Fed a spell slot, it makes a persistent faerie fire cloud for a minute, with a radius of 10, 20 or 30 feet by slot, with no concentration and no save.
It is a non-Weave conduit, so it works inside an anti-magic field.
The Tyrant Ship's Collection Manifest lists it as entry 051, from the outer Kellis Belt: intake, unprocessed.

nodes.label: Flighty Foundling
nodes.summary: A Caelestis hammerhead.

facts.t: The Flighty Foundling brings Ezra out to the crew at the swap.
It supplies the scuttle ship that docks in the Tyrant Ship's Cargo intake for shore parties.

nodes.label: H'Catha
nodes.summary: A toroidal beholder sea-world with the Spindle at its center.

facts.t: H'Catha is the crew's first world beyond Caelestis, and Vecna stays faint there.
Vecna's hand on H'Catha reaches back to its founding, and a residue of his worship lingers.
One of H'Catha's eldest rulers may know something of Vecna's hand there.
Each domain's terrain carries its ruler's signature ray, soaked in over ages.
Free locathah, guides and exiles live on the seams between domains.
Only one of the mercane in its ports works for Vocath.
H'Catha has ten domains, one for each eyestalk, each with one enlightened ruler, under the Sovereign Eye.

nodes.label: The Sovereign Eye
nodes.summary: The presence the rulers of H'Catha dreamt together, which sees everything in daylight and enforces the Pact.

facts.t: The Sovereign Eye sees everything in daylight and enforces the Pact; shadow is its blind spot.
Vecna influenced the making of the Sovereign Eye, hoping its dreaming would bring H'Catha to a Zenith. It did not.

nodes.label: The Spindle
nodes.summary: The structure at the center of H'Catha that drew the beholders there.

facts.t: The beholders gathered on H'Catha drawn by the Spindle.
Magic grows unreliable the higher one climbs the Spindle.

nodes.label: Kurrzot
nodes.summary: A beholder ruler of H'Catha, a claimant to the meteor.

facts.t: He claims the meteor that struck the Pupil on the seam between his domain and his rival's.
He sends an emissary rather than an attack over his unsettled business with Vaelorix.

nodes.label: The H'Catha meteor
nodes.summary: An adamantine meteor that struck beside the Spindle.

facts.t: The meteor is adamantine and hums on the same frequency as Boogie's shard and Gregory's core.
It struck the Pupil, on the seam between Kurrzot's domain and his rival's, and is mined as a vein in an occupied, skirmished area.
Adamantine matters on H'Catha because the Sovereign Eye cannot see through it.

nodes.label: Tumak Swan
nodes.summary: Twin halflings, Wan and Tu, passing as one person.

facts.t: Tumak is twin halflings, Wan and Tu, two hosts passing as one person.
Both twins are partial Wayfinders of the Runekeepers, Lunarfoot clan.
The Dissolution fragment is forming in both twins, half a rune to each.
When both twins arrive home, the stalled cycle brings a Zenith and ends the concealment.
Tumak has his own Heart-rune.
He met the previous Runekeeper once, briefly, and does not understand what that meeting was.
He wants his home.

nodes.label: Casey Geim
nodes.summary: A hadozee warlock and Starchild whose patron he knows as his brother.

facts.t: The voice Casey hears as Polly is Astra Virex wearing Polly's shape, and it grows clearer with each tether.
Casey is a younger brother who does not know his full identity, and he clings to Tumak as an older brother.
He is a Starchild who sees constellations nobody else can.
Every tether he makes anchors Astra Virex into another region, and the region pays the cost.
His first tether point is Virenspace, already altered by Zerathis.
He wants his brother.

nodes.label: Gregory
nodes.summary: An autognome wizard who casts.

facts.t: Gregory's awakening is a result of the Axiom strain's ripple.
He comes from the Cogfast Enclave on Lantan, on Toril.
He senses paracausal events as a felt pull, and the pull led him to the Lantern.
The Lantern's sealed source calls past him rather than to him.

nodes.label: Boogie
nodes.summary: A plasmoid sorcerer carrying a shard of the Fonains Monolith in his nucleus.

facts.t: The urge to dance is the Pulse of the Fonains shard in his nucleus.
Tharizdun wants nothing specific from Boogie, and what comes through the shard depends on what Boogie does.
He sometimes feels corruption leaking into him from the shard.
He wants to belong to something.

nodes.label: Bartholomew Grayson
nodes.summary: A Rashemi Circle of the Stars druid and wilder.

facts.t: Bartholomew wants the peace within him, his constellation.
He is a wilder.
His constellation is CON-312.
He is circling a shape he has not taken, the Almost, and his slips toward it match none of his beast forms or his Starry Form.
His druidic tradition was pointed at the sky before he reached Caelestis.

nodes.label: Sol Fortuna
nodes.summary: An astral elf paladin of Beshaba, escaped from Aethris.

facts.t: The Fortuned want Sol back alive because he is a component of their unfinished ritual.
He left Aethris before the ritual closed: a Watcher of the Order extracted him, and the Order broke protocol to recommend him to Caelestis.
He bears the Oath of Misfortune.
Aethris shows what other worlds are being aimed toward, and Sol is the one who walked out of it.

nodes.label: CON-312
nodes.summary: The constellation in Bartholomew's chest.

facts.t: CON-312 lies at bearing 312° in Caelestis's sky.
Its number is an old catalogue number that it carried before the crew found it.

nodes.label: Polly Geim
nodes.summary: Casey's brother, changed at a fallen star and missing.

facts.t: A star fell on Polly's world; he went to it, was changed, and left to find where it came from.
The real Polly was consumed, or is caught between life and death.
Astra Virex wears Polly's voice to reach Casey.
The real Polly was consumed, or is caught between life and death; no one knows which.
The voice Casey hears as Polly is Astra Virex wearing his shape.

nodes.label: Zerathis
nodes.summary: A spellcaster and prior Starchild, dissolved into Virenspace.

facts.t: Zerathis was a Starchild who tethered to Virenspace repeatedly and took every gift Astra Virex offered.
His identity dissolved into the system's paracausal layer, and what remains still speaks.
The wardrobe he gave Mirt is one of his tethers.
Zerathis followed Astra Virex and was no part of Vecna's following.

nodes.label: Mirt's Wardrobe
nodes.summary: Mirt's extradimensional wardrobe.

facts.t: The wardrobe is a paracausal replica of Zerathis's anchor site, carrying a thread of the Viren shift across space.
It is why Casey was drawn to it, and why Astra Virex could reach him there in Polly's voice.
The sky inside it is CON-055, as seen from Virenspace.

nodes.label: Viren Star System
nodes.summary: Virenspace: an overlap site that speaks in a dead Starchild's voice.

facts.t: Virenspace is an overlap site where paracausal change runs faster than a single tether would make it.
What is at Viren now is part Zerathis, part Astra's reach and part the site.

nodes.label: The Runekeepers
nodes.summary: A hidden order of Wayfinders on an unfindable world.

facts.t: The Runekeepers practise Wayfinding, attuning to places and through them to their hearts; the Lunarfoot clan is among them.
Their travel is not Weave-based, so Forbiddance does not stop it.
A Wayfinder can attune only to bodies that have a heart.
Exiled Wayfinders are given no map and no name, and must recognize home through remembered fragments.

nodes.label: The Runekeeper
nodes.summary: The living practitioner whose body holds the homeworld's concealment.

facts.t: The Runekeeper bears the inscription that withdraws the Wayfinders' homeworld from cosmological visibility.
He is dimming as the Dissolution fragment leaves him for Wan and Tu.
His fade runs on a soft clock: rising pressure, no date.
Neither he nor the order knows the fragment is Reach residue.
He is the only permitted way into and out of the homeworld, and he sent Wan and Tu out himself.
A Runekeeper's death is celebrated: “We do not mourn this. We sing.”

nodes.label: The Wayfinders' homeworld
nodes.summary: A halfling world in GAL-01, hidden by a living ritual and nameless by doctrine.

facts.t: The world sits where it has always sat, and finding it means knowing the way back rather than the coordinates.
It shares a galaxy with the threats its Wayfinders map.
Lunarfoot is the clan, not the world.

nodes.label: Cogfast Enclave
nodes.summary: An enclave on Lantan, on Toril.

facts.t: The Cogfast Enclave on Lantan, on Toril, is where Gregory comes from.

nodes.label: Toril
nodes.summary: The principal world of Realmspace.

facts.t: Toril gives Realmspace its name.

nodes.label: Realmspace
nodes.summary: The home system.

facts.t: Realmspace lies in GAL-01, and Caelestis orbits Toril there.

nodes.label: Aethris
nodes.summary: Sol's Tymora-devoted homeworld, past its Zenith.

facts.t: Aethris sorts its people into the Fortuned and the Misfortuned.
Aethris's Zenith came in Cycle 1490; what stands incomplete is the Fortuned's ritual.
Vecna is pushing the Fortuned's ritual toward completion from outside, and nobody on Aethris knows it.

nodes.label: The Prism Ascendant
nodes.summary: The Monolith that answered Aethris's Zenith.

facts.t: The Prism Ascendant has archived what it can and stays where it is; it does nothing.
Aethris holds that the Prism Ascendant is Tymora's answer to the ritual.

nodes.label: The Fortuned
nodes.summary: A sect grown from a temple order of Tymora on Aethris, mostly clerics, whose ritual brought Aethris to its Zenith and stands incomplete.

facts.t: The Fortuned want Sol back as a component of their ritual and do not care about him as a person.
The Fortuned commissioned the Crystalline Retrieval Construct after Sol's escape.
Long ago the Fortuned cast a generational curse that made a group of people gather their misfortune: the Misfortuned.
They are led by a priest or priestess and are not the rulers of the whole world.
They dress in pristine robes of white and gold.

nodes.label: Crystalline Retrieval Construct
nodes.summary: A construct built to capture and return Sol.

facts.t: The construct's assignment is capture, correction and return, and it never taunts.
Its face slowly resolves into a perfect mirror of Sol's.
It is built to retrieve rather than kill, and it remembers the damage that hurt it.
Its first encounter with the crew is at the Caelestis main entrance, on their return from H'Catha.
It tracks Sol by resonance and cannot keep pace with a spelljammer in transit.

nodes.label: Fonains
nodes.summary: The world of Lola's Boys, CSC 16423 c in Krynnspace, whose corrupted Monolith Lola's Boys broke.

facts.t: Fonains and Krynn share a system in GAL-01.
Caelestis's present sits level with Fonains Session 28, two to three months after its Monolith broke.
Thessalar's planar craft crashed on Fonains about five hundred years ago.
The crash is how the Elder Elemental Eye reached Fonains, and Tharizdun's influence spread from the fallen temple.
Most of Fonains's dragons left to face Takhisis, and Fonains remembers it as a great hunt.

nodes.label: The Fonains Monolith
nodes.summary: A corrupted Monolith, the only one ever destroyed.

facts.t: Fonains's Monolith is the only one recorded as destroyed.
It formed corrupted, and Tharizdun's crystal replicated into it as it formed.
When it broke, four great shards fell and many smaller shards came from them.
Three hundred and thirty-three of the small shards are black; the rest took colours near their elemental affinities.

nodes.label: The Fonains shard
nodes.summary: A shard of the Fonains Monolith, inside Boogie's nucleus.

facts.t: The shard is Monolith matter, not residue.
It is still attempting to archive on a very small scale.
It came from Fonains through Vocath's Cairn Station line, and Boogie took it from a shipment.

nodes.label: The five-person ritual
nodes.summary: The Zenith that raised the Fonains Monolith.

facts.t: Four cultists channelled the Princes and the fifth held pieces of a Tharizdun artifact.
The ritual was Fonains's Zenith, nudged by Vecna.

nodes.label: The Darkest Day
nodes.summary: The eclipse when the Monolith erupted over the cemetery.

facts.t: Vecna's cult worked a ritual on Giorge at the eclipse, as bait.
The Monolith erupted over the cemetery, and the first Accordance champions died fighting it.

nodes.label: The Monolith breaks
nodes.summary: Kwalish's cannon splits the Fonains Monolith.

facts.t: Kwalish's cannon split the Monolith into four shards, each guarded by a Prince-aligned elemental.
Tharizdun said to wait for the day of chaos.

nodes.label: The Day of Chaos
nodes.summary: When the Princes break the barriers so Tharizdun can leave her prison.

facts.t: The Day of Chaos is when the Princes of Elemental Evil break the barriers so Tharizdun can leave her prison.
The four Princes are to enter Fonains together.

nodes.label: The Princes of Elemental Evil
nodes.summary: Imix, Olhydra, Ogrémoch and Yan-C-Bin.

facts.t: About twelve thousand years ago the Princes rose on Fonains and the Accordance sealed them away.
The crew meets the Princes' pressure as strange elemental phenomena on the worlds they visit.
Tharizdun's cults raised the Princes' four prophets.

nodes.label: Imix
nodes.summary: The Prince of Elemental Fire.

facts.t: About three and a half centuries ago a fire genasi sect tried to summon Imix.
The price of sealing him again was that Imix be forgotten.

nodes.label: Olhydra
nodes.summary: The Princess of Elemental Water.

facts.t: Olhydra and Ogrémoch collided, and the planar craft's gems formed where they met.

nodes.label: Ogrémoch
nodes.summary: The Prince of Elemental Earth.

facts.t: The collision of Olhydra and Ogrémoch carved the waterway under what became the Temple of Moloch.

nodes.label: Yan-C-Bin
nodes.summary: The Prince of Elemental Air.

facts.t: Yan-C-Bin is manifest on Fonains at Session 28.

nodes.label: Tinderstrike
nodes.summary: The fire key, bound to the Cre'Tez blood.

facts.t: Asmodeus gave Tinderstrike to the few fire genasi who resisted Imix, and bound the key to their blood.
It is held by the Cre'Tez line in the Eternal Flame temple.
Asmodus needs every birthright to claim it, and Vanifer waits to take it from whoever does.

nodes.label: The war pick
nodes.summary: The earth key.

facts.t: The Sacred Stone took the war pick from the dwarven vault under the Martyr Dome.

nodes.label: The air spear
nodes.summary: The air key.

facts.t: Aerisi Kalinoth took the spear from Eldath's tree in the Misty Vale.
With it she called forth Yan-C-Bin.

nodes.label: The trident
nodes.summary: The water key.

facts.t: The trident was sealed in a living coral reef grown over a sunken craft, guarded by the Thessalkraken.
Gar Shatterkeel holds it and hears a voice in the water.
